advances: A regular positive-buffer structure theorem for a single independently tested planar fiber.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
By the regular singleton formula, the nonconstant smooth part has Hessian
$$
\nabla^2G(X)=A+\sum_{i:p_i=z}\frac{4\eta_i\delta_i}{E_i}P_i(X)^{-5}a_i a_i^{\mathsf T}.
$$
Each $P_i(X)=1+a_i\cdot(X-y_i)$ in this expression is strictly positive on a common neighborhood of the compact fiber. Thus $G$ is analytic and convex there. Use pk-w34-buffered-planar-facet-convex-order on the bounded Borel density and the stated convex tests. A facet on which $W$ is constant almost everywhere has a continuous convex representative of $\Xi|_F$, namely that constant plus $G+c$. Use this representative as the one-dimensional facet test. The result is $\int_F\Xi^2\,ds\le0$. The representative vanishes, and its zero tangential second derivative in the displayed sum forces the orthogonality assertions.

A facet whose relative interior meets no proper cap line has constant profile almost everywhere, since strict full or empty terms are constant and the regular supporting traces have zero arclength. If $A$ is positive definite, the tangential Hessian is positive, so every facet is met in its relative interior by a proper cap line. Each proper line meets the planar convex boundary in two endpoints and cannot contain a facet. Each such intersection lies in the relative interior of at most one facet, yielding the $2m$ bound. Remove the finitely many closed facets and all proper line intersection points. The profile is constant on each remaining arc and the decomposition makes $\Xi=0$ arclength-almost everywhere there. By continuity of $G$ and positive length of every nontrivial open subarc, this gives $G=-c-W$ throughout the arc. A stationary point of the strictly convex $G$ on its convex domain of positivity would be its strict minimum, so none lies on a nontrivial constant-level arc. The analytic implicit-function theorem then gives an analytic curve, with positive curvature magnitude equal to the tangential Hessian divided by $\lVert\nabla G\rVert$. At common curved endpoints, continuity forces the constants on both sides to agree. Hence their profile jumps cancel, and if the boundary is facetless all constants coincide around the boundary.

If $A$ has rank one, all positively weighted $u_{ij}$ lie in its range. The exact source balance $\sum_j\rho_{ij}u_{ij}=\varepsilon(E_i/M)^{1/3}a_i$ puts every present positively weighted $a_i$ in the same line. Hence $G$ is a strictly convex function of the scalar coordinate in that line. Its level sets lie on at most two lines perpendicular to the range of $A$. Any facet with no interior crossing is parallel to $\ker A$ by the tangential assertion, so at most two such maximal facets occur. The other facets number at most $2m$ as above. If their closed union did not exhaust the boundary, some remaining open subarc would avoid all finitely many crossings, hence lie in one of the level lines by the same continuity argument. A nontrivial such segment belongs to a maximal facet, a contradiction. The body is a polygon.
statement: Consider a planar fiber $K_z$ with the regular singleton covariance-buffer density of cf17d6bf1aab7a2d at positive $\varepsilon$, and choose nonnegative group weights $\eta_i$. Write $\Xi=W+G+c$ on this fiber, where $W=\sum_{ij}\eta_i\theta_{ij}\kappa_{ij}$ is its finite closed-cap profile, $G$ is the sum of its positive projective and quadratic terms, and $c$ is its constant term. Let $m$ count the distinct proper cap lines with positive coefficient on this fiber and put $A=M^{-1}\sum_{ij}\eta_i\delta_i\rho_{ij}u_{ij}u_{ij}^{\mathsf T}$. Assume $\int_{\partial K_z}\Xi\Phi\,ds\le0$ for every finite continuous convex $\Phi$ on the plane. On each facet with $W$ constant almost everywhere, $\Xi=0$ almost everywhere, and every positively weighted continuous normal and every positively weighted present own projective parameter is orthogonal to its tangent. If $A$ is positive definite, there are at most $2m$ facets. Off the closed facets and cap-line crossing points, each nontrivial boundary arc is part of an analytic level curve $G=-c-W$ of strictly positive curvature. At a point joining curved arcs without a facet between them the weighted profile jumps cancel. If there are no facets, the entire boundary lies on one level. If $A$ has rank one, the fiber is a polygon with at most $2m+2$ facets.
title: Finite facets and analytic arcs for a freely tested planar buffered density
